purpose: Second experiment-calibrated sample16 AC3D SIP candidate after partial all-mechanism diagnostics.

relationship_to_v1.evidence: The v1 y-direction all-mechanism diagnostic matched real conductivity well but placed the imaginary-conductivity relaxation too low in frequency: low-frequency sigma'' was too high and high-frequency sigma'' was too low.
relationship_to_v1.change: Keep the successful DC/background conductivity setting and reduce the effective membrane polarization length scale to move the relaxation toward higher frequency.

rationale.solid_conductivity_s_m: Retain 0.0024 S/m because v1 y-direction maxwell and all diagnostics match the experimental real-conductivity baseline within about 3-9 percent.
rationale.surface_conductance_s: Retain 1.5e-10 S for this test so that the next diagnostic isolates the relaxation-time shift before retuning amplitude.
rationale.membrane_polarizability_eta0: Retain 0.0013 for this test so amplitude changes can be attributed mostly to the membrane-length correction.
rationale.membrane_length_scale: Set to 0.1 as an experimental-calibration diagnostic. Since tau_m scales with L^2, this shifts the membrane relaxation roughly two decades higher in frequency, which is the direction required by the v1 diagnostic.
rationale.status: This is a calibrated sensitivity candidate, not the strict sample16 formal geometry-scale-1 run.

diagnostic_plan.decision_rule: If real conductivity remains near the experiment and sigma'' shifts upward toward the experimental high-frequency rise without large low-frequency overprediction, use this family for the full 51-frequency sweep; otherwise scan membrane_length_scale around 0.05-0.2 before a full run.
